Jaundice.description: Jaundice is a yellowing of the skin and eyes caused by a buildup of bilirubin, often linked to liver, gallbladder, or blood disorders.
Jaundice.treatment: Treatment targets the underlying cause and may include fluids, dietary changes, or medication; a doctor should evaluate liver and bile function.

Alzheimers.description: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive neurological disorder causing memory loss, confusion, and behavioral changes.
Alzheimers.treatment: There is no cure; care focuses on medications that ease symptoms, structured routines, and support from caregivers and specialists.

Arthritis.description: Arthritis is inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain and stiffness that often worsens with age.
Arthritis.treatment: Management includes anti-inflammatory medication, physical therapy, gentle exercise, and weight management.

Tuberculosis.description: Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection that primarily affects the lungs, spreading through airborne droplets.
Tuberculosis.treatment: Treatment requires a several-month course of prescribed antibiotics under medical supervision to fully clear the infection.

Asthma.description: Asthma is a chronic condition in which airways narrow and swell, making breathing difficult and often triggering coughing or wheezing.
Asthma.treatment: Inhaled bronchodilators and anti-inflammatory medication help control symptoms; avoiding known triggers reduces flare-ups.

Sinusitis.description: Sinusitis is inflammation of the sinus cavities, often following a cold, causing facial pressure and congestion.
Sinusitis.treatment: Saline rinses, decongestants, and rest usually help; bacterial cases may need antibiotics if symptoms persist.

Epilepsy.description: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder marked by recurrent seizures caused by abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
Epilepsy.treatment: Anti-seizure medication prescribed by a neurologist is the primary treatment, alongside lifestyle adjustments to reduce triggers.

Heart Disease.description: Heart disease covers a range of conditions affecting the heart, including narrowed arteries that can lead to chest pain or heart attack.
Heart Disease.treatment: Treatment may include lifestyle changes, medication to manage blood pressure and cholesterol, and in some cases surgery.

Diabetes.description: Diabetes is a metabolic condition where the body cannot properly regulate blood sugar levels.
Diabetes.treatment: Management involves monitoring blood sugar, dietary changes, and medication such as insulin or oral drugs as prescribed.

Glaucoma.description: Glaucoma is a group of eye conditions that damage the optic nerve, often linked to elevated eye pressure.
Glaucoma.treatment: Prescription eye drops, laser therapy, or surgery can lower eye pressure and help prevent vision loss.

Hyperthyroidism.description: Hyperthyroidism occurs when the thyroid gland produces excess hormone, speeding up the body's metabolism.
Hyperthyroidism.treatment: Treatment options include anti-thyroid medication, beta-blockers for symptom relief, radioactive iodine, or surgery.

Heat Stroke.description: Heat stroke is a severe heat-related illness where the body's core temperature rises dangerously high, impairing normal function.
Heat Stroke.treatment: This is a medical emergency requiring immediate cooling and fluids; seek emergency care right away.

Hypothermia.description: Hypothermia occurs when the body loses heat faster than it can produce it, causing dangerously low body temperature.
Hypothermia.treatment: Gradual rewarming, dry insulation, and warm fluids are needed; severe cases require emergency medical care.

Coronavirus.description: Coronavirus (COVID-19) is a viral respiratory infection that spreads through respiratory droplets and can range from mild to severe.
Coronavirus.treatment: Rest, fluids, and symptom management are typical for mild cases; seek medical care if breathing difficulty or high fever persists.
